# DIY Investing Course

> A free, self-paced educational course about investing for yourself. The course has 27 lessons in 9 modules, an interactive glossary, a hypothetical compound-growth sandbox, browser-only progress tracking, and permanent shareable lesson pages. No account or email is required.

## Canonical course
- Home and interactive course: https://diyinvestingcourse.com/
- Complete curriculum and FAQ: https://diyinvestingcourse.com/#curriculum
- Searchable investing glossary: https://diyinvestingcourse.com/#glossary
- Official-source resource library: https://diyinvestingcourse.com/#resources
- XML sitemap: https://diyinvestingcourse.com/sitemap.xml

## Authoritative primary sources
- U.S. investor education and verification: https://www.investor.gov/
- U.S. public-company filings: https://www.sec.gov/edgar/search-and-access
- U.S. broker background checks: https://brokercheck.finra.org/
- Current U.S. federal tax rules: https://www.irs.gov/
- 2026 U.S. IRA and workplace-plan contribution-limit announcement: https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/401k-limit-increases-to-24500-for-2026-ira-limit-increases-to-7500
- U.S. securities settlement (T+1): https://www.sec.gov/resources-for-investors/investor-alerts-bulletins/new-t1-settlement-cycle-what-investors-need-know-investor-bulletin
- Deposit insurance information: https://www.fdic.gov/resources/deposit-insurance/
- U.S. Treasury securities: https://www.treasurydirect.gov/
- Federal Reserve economic data: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/

## Important context
- The material is general education, not individualized investment, tax, or legal advice and not a recommendation to buy or sell a security. Investing involves risk, including possible loss of principal. No returns are promised.
- Most account, tax, and market-structure examples use U.S. rules. Readers elsewhere should consult their own regulator, tax authority, and account terms.
- Contribution limits and laws change; the retirement-limit example is explicitly for 2026. Verify the relevant tax year with the current IRS source before acting.
- The site provides educational frameworks rather than live market data, stock picks, or return forecasts. Browser-stored progress is optional, local to the visitor's device, and not tied to an account.
